title: Arafah at home
hookLine: fasting and du'a on the day of Arafah
tomorrow: a father, a son, a ram: what was really given?

cards: A graduation is streaming live. Halfway across the world, a grandmother who couldn't fly in is watching from her kitchen, dressed up anyway, as if she were in the front row.
On the day of Arafah, the pilgrims stand on a wide plain outside Mecca, praying. And everyone else? They aren't just watching.
In Sahih Muslim, the Prophet ﷺ is asked about fasting this day, and he says: I hope from God that it wipes away the year before it and the year after.

teach.h: CAN YOU JOIN A DAY ELSEWHERE?
teach.b: So today's question: can you take part in a day that's happening somewhere else? Islam's answer is yes, in a different way. On the plain, the pilgrims stand and pray.
At home, people fast and make du'a, and a hadith in Tirmidhi calls the du'a of the day of Arafah the best du'a. One to tell a friend: the pilgrims themselves don't fast it.

People once weren't sure whether the Prophet was fasting at Arafah, so Umm al-Fadl sent him a cup of milk, and he drank it in front of everyone. One day, two places, two ways in. Jews know a day like this.

teach.h: YOM KIPPUR: A DAY TO BE CLEANSED.
teach.b: Yom Kippur, the Day of Atonement, is a fast given over to asking forgiveness.
The Torah says, in the 1917 Jewish Publication Society translation: "For on this day shall atonement be made for you, to cleanse you; from all your sins shall ye be clean before the LORD."
What's shared is real: one day set apart, an empty stomach, and a long, honest asking to be made clean. And an honest difference.
In the Torah, the Yom Kippur fast is commanded for the whole people.
The Arafah fast is voluntary, kept by those at home, while the pilgrims stand instead.

how: On the day of Arafah, within the first ten days of Dhul Hijjah, pilgrims stand in prayer on the plain of Arafah while Muslims at home keep a voluntary fast and spend the day in du'a.

o: a prayer said at home on the night before the Hajj
fasting and du'a at home on the pilgrims' great day
visiting the pilgrims' plain on any day of the year

games.q: who does what on the day — tap the pairs.
p: stand and pray on the plain

s: pilgrims standing at Arafah are expected to fast that day
the Prophet drank milk in front of people at Arafah; the fast is kept by those at home.
Jews also keep a fast day given to atonement
Yom Kippur. Leviticus 16:30: on this day shall atonement be made for you.
the Arafah fast and Yom Kippur are one thing under two names
both are fasts for forgiveness; Yom Kippur's is commanded for the whole people, Arafah's is voluntary, at home.

games.q: your friend is on Hajj and texts from the plain on the day of Arafah: should she be fasting today, like her mom back home?
o: yes: the Arafah fast is for everyone, pilgrims first of all.
no: on the plain the standing and du'a are the day; the fast is for home.
only if she's strong enough to go without water in the heat.
games.why: when people weren't sure, Umm al-Fadl sent the Prophet a cup of milk at Arafah, and he drank it in front of them. the pilgrims stand; those at home fast.

practice: Stand up where you are, feet planted, hands open at your sides, the way the pilgrims stand on the plain. Stay standing for the sit.
If you make du'a, this is a time for it; if not, hold in mind one thing you'd like to be forgiven for, or one person you'd like to forgive.

wordCard.voice: Arafah at home: the pilgrims' great day, kept from far away with a fast and du'a. One day, two places.

orig.note: Arabic: the plain outside Mecca where the pilgrims stand, and the day named for it.

carryVoice: Here's the line: standing at home, fasting while the pilgrims stand. The plain is far, the day is near.

Sahih al-Bukhari 1988 (Umm al-Fadl sends milk to the Prophet at Arafah; he drinks it)
